newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission adopts Eco-label reform proposals.
newsitem.headline: Commission adopts Eco-label reform proposals.

text.p: The European Commission adopted on Tuesday a proposal for a regulation to amend the troubled eco-label rules in Regulation 880/92.

"Certain difficulties have been encountered in the implementation of the Regulation and there is a need for improving and streamlining the approach, methodologies and working procedures of the scheme, in order to increase its effectiveness, efficiency and transparency," said the document's explanatory memorandum.
It suggested that the existing "pass-fail" system for awarding the eco-label logo be revamped to allow a grading system for each quantitative criteria considered for each applicant product.

It also proposed reducing Commission involvement in the routine, highly specialised technical work required for assessing product criteria by setting up a European Eco-Label Organisation (EEO) to coordinate the activities of member states' eco-label bodies.
The EEO, a private international association of the eco-label bodies, would work under Commission mandate and surveillance -- similar to the way the European Standardization Committee (CEN) operates.

The revision would also seek to ensure "complementarity" between the EU scheme and those in member states, set a maximum annual fee for using the label and make the scheme comply with international trade rules.
